Yes. So the Preventing Maternal Best Act was really that first step in addressing the maternal mortality health crisis. But we're working on other pieces that are going to build on this. I have a new maternal health bill called Excellence in Maternal Health. And it's bipartisan. These are all bipartisan because, believe it or not, health problems impact
everybody. They don't know

a party. But this bill sets up new grants to address maternal health and build on our old piece. So some of the highlights are it's going to put together grants for people to help who are improving maternal health care quality and they're going to be eliminating prevent maternal mortality and severe maternal morbidity. That's the other piece. People don't realize, so the numbers I had given earlier, seven to nine hundred women do die every year. That's the mortality number, but the severe maternal morbidity, the close calls, is through the roof. So we're trying to get at some of the prevention to avoid getting into the place where women are experiencing this morbidity. And I'm also working on a number of child care bills. So I started the maternal health caucus with a Democrat from down in California, Lucille Royville-Allard a couple years ago. We've had some big wins. You know, the childcare piece is another area where we're starting to look at. In Washington State and Southwest Washington, they call it a childcare desert. So the number of quality providers is completely dwindled and people are really struggling to find affordable care for their kiddos. So there's a few different pieces of legislation that we're working on with the caucus and then as the Congress as a whole to address this. So there's a number of pieces I think are going to be benefiting families, working families across the board and I'm really excited about it.
